record.original_question: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the bi-Lagrangi an Grassmannian LG(V, J ) to be a smooth algebraic variety. Describe the partition of LG(V, J ) into Aut(V, J )-orbits. A "non-linear analog" of the existence of bi-Lagrangian subspaces would be the existence of complete subalgebras F ⊂ C∞ (M ) consisting of functions in involution with respect to all the bracket s from a given Poisson pencil. By completeness in this case we mean that the s ubspace generated by the differentials of functions f ∈ F in the cotangent space T ∗ x M is maximal isotropic. It is natural to refer to such a subalgebra (or to a collection of its generators) as a bi-integrable system. In the case of Kronecker pencils, such a subalgebra F is generated by the (local) Casimir functions of the brackets in the pencil. It is well known that F so obtained is complete and commutative with respect to all the brackets in the pencil ([20, 83]). Similar results in t he symplectic case are due to P. Olver [176] and H. Turiel [216]. In the mixed case (when the Jord an-Kronecker decomposition of a pencil includes both Kronecker and Jordan blocks), bi-integra ble systems do exist locally in a neighbourhood of a generic point. However, to the best of our kno wledge, this result has never been published. In view of the above discussion on the partition of LG( V, J ) into different orbits, it would be natural to distinguish bi-integrable systems of different algebraic types. Mo re precisely, let f1,..., fk be a complete set of functions in bi-involution. We restrict our considera tions to a small neighbourhood U of a generic point x ∈ M such that for each y ∈ U the Jordan-Kronecker type of the pencil defined on T ∗ y M by a pair of compatible Poisson brackets is the same. If we think of T ∗ y M as a bi-Poisson vector space, then the subspace Ly = span{d f1(y),..., d fk(y)} ⊂ T ∗ y M is bi-Lagrangian and therefore can be characterised by its algebraic type (i.e., by the type of the orbits of the automorphism group action in the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian to which L belongs). If this type remains the same for all points y ∈ U, we refer to it as the algebraic type of the bi-integrable system f1,..., fk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, and let $J = \{\omega_\lambda = \omega_0 + \lambda \omega_\infty\}_{\lambda \in \mathbb{P}^1}$ be a pencil of skew-symmetric bilinear forms on $V$ (so $(V,J)$ is a bi-Poisson vector space). A subspace $L \subset V$ is called bi-Lagrangian if it is maximal isotropic with respect to every form in the pencil $J$. Denote by $LG(V,J)$ the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian, i.e. the set of all bi-Lagrangian subspaces, viewed as an algebraic subvariety of an appropriate Lagrangian Grassmannian. Let $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$ be the group of linear automorphisms of $V$ preserving the pencil $J$.

(a) Find necessary and sufficient conditions, in terms of the Jordan–Kronecker invariants of the pencil $J$, for the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian $LG(V,J)$ to be a smooth algebraic variety.

(b) Describe the partition of $LG(V,J)$ into orbits of the natural action of $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint by I. K. Kozlov, "Geometry of bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian" (arXiv:2409.09855), addresses precisely these questions: it computes dimensions, describes the open orbit, and gives a complete description of Aut(V,J)-orbits in several cases (a single Jordan block, sums of equal Jordan blocks, sums of two distinct Jordan blocks), with partial topological/dimension results in general (Theorem 11.6). A full classification of orbits and complete smoothness criteria for arbitrary Jordan–Kronecker type do not yet appear to be established, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian
status_evidence.snippet: Unlike Lagrangian Grassmannians, a bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian has a natural structure of an algebraic variety. Dimension is calculated and the open orbit under the automorphism group is described. Aut(V,P)-orbits are completely described in three cases: one Jordan block, sums of equal Jordan blocks, and sums of two distinct Jordan blocks.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results on smoothness and orbit decomposition of LG(V,J) are obtained by Kozlov (2024).
